rule.title: Strict Zero-Any Policy in TypeScript
rule.statement: The 'any' keyword is strictly prohibited in application code. Use unknown, generics, or explicit narrowing types.
rule.rationale: Using 'any' silently disables the TypeScript type checker, propagating unsafety across callers and causing preventable runtime crashes.
rule.implementation_guidance: Enable @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: 'error'. Use type guards (if (typeof x === 'string')) to narrow unknown.

forbidden.example: function parse(input: any): any { return input.name; } // Type-unsafe

preferred.example: function parse(input: unknown): string { if (typeof input === 'string') return input; throw new Error(); }

source.section: Item 1: Understand the Relationship Between TypeScript and JavaScript
source.evidence_quote: The any type silences the type checker and your tooling. It undermines confidence in the system and hides bugs until runtime.
